title: Runtime probe harness for kernel selector & attention latency mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
We need a focused probe harness to exercise the runtime's kernel selector and attention pathways across real prefill/decode traffic shapes, and to produce high-fidelity NVTX ranges + trace spans with per-kernel metrics. Existing telemetry captures kernel attribution broadly, but we lack: 1) deterministic micro-benchmarks that reproduce selector decisions, 2) a stable naming envelope for NVTX ranges that can be correlated to span-level aggregates, and 3) per-kernel resource signals (e.g., tensor-core utilization, occupancy, stall reasons) that are easy to join with request-level traces.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Implement a probe harness that can replay representative prefill and decode request mixes (short chat turns, long-context summarization, streaming decode) with configurable micro-batch sizes and kv-cache reuse patterns.
- Emit NVTX ranges with a new canonical envelope: "rw:exec:<phase>:<kernel_family>:<kernel_variant>:<exec_id>" and attach span tags that include kernel_choice, seq_len, batch_size, kv_hit_ratio.
- Export per-kernel metrics for: kernel_exec_ms, kernel_queue_ms, tensor_core_util_pct, sm_occupancy_pct, memory_bandwidth_bytes, warps_active, stall_reason_counts. These must be exposed to Prometheus and attached to trace spans in Datadog/Tempo.
- Produce a comparison dashboard (prefill vs decode) demonstrating how kernel selection changes with sequence length and batch size and showing end-to-end latency attribution to kernels.
- Create reproducible benchmarks and a PR that adds the harness and a sample dashboard.

Technical approach:
1) Harness: a small Go/Python binary (prototype in Python) that can issue multi-phase traffic: prefill-only, decode-only, and combined flows. Each flow parameterized by seq_len, micro_batch, kv_reuse_percent, and attention-type (causal vs masked). The harness should annotate each request with a trace id and attach a synthetic request tag to make post-aggregation filtering trivial.
2) NVTX and span envelope: standardize names to "rw:exec" prefix. Implement a thin wrapper in the runtime instrumentation layer that composes NVTX ranges and span tags atomically (so we do not end up with desynced NVTX->span mappings under sampling).
3) Per-kernel metrics: add lightweight samplers in the kernel launch path that record start_ns/end_ns, kernel_id, kernel_family, sm_utilization_percent (via CUPTI or perf API), and memory_bandwidth_bytes for the duration. Aggregate into rolling histograms and expose via Prometheus metrics with labels kernel_family, kernel_variant, seq_len_bucket.
4) Dashboard & eval: add Grafana/Datadog dashboard panels for kernel-level latency heatmaps, kernel_selection frequency matrix (seq_len x batch_size), and cumulative latency waterfall for an example request.

Design trade-offs / Notes:
- Sampling frequency vs overhead: we will sample 1:10 by default for production but run full-capture during dedicated test runs. The probe harness will include flags for full_capture=true for isolated nodes.
- CUPTI vs lightweight counters: CUPTI gives richer GPU-side data but is higher overhead and harder to deploy in multi-tenant Dedicated. We will abstract the collector so we can toggle between CUPTI and a lower-overhead estimator based on SM counters.
- Naming stability: make the NVTX envelope stable across releases; changes require a migration note in release notes and dashboard updates.

Implementation plan / Milestones:
- 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-13: prototype harness and NVTX envelope in a branch (completed).
- 2026-03-14 to 2026-03-17: implement per-kernel sampler and Prometheus exporter; add span enrichment logic.
- 2026-03-18: open PR for runtime + harness with unit/integration tests.
- 2026-03-19: review feedback, iterate.
- 2026-03-20: land PR and deploy to staging, run probe harness, populate dashboard sample data.

Risks and mitigations:
- Overhead in hotpath: ensure default sampling and off-by-default full capture. Measure p50/p99 regression on microbench harness.
- Telemetry cardinality explosion: bucket seq_len and batch_size (e.g., seq_len: [<=64,65-256,257-1024,>1024]) to keep metrics cardinality manageable.
- Cross-system joins: ensure trace id propagation to Prometheus labels via a short-lived mapping service for diagnostics only (avoid injecting trace ids into metrics normally).

Test plan:
- Unit tests for NVTX string formatting and span-tag mapping.
- Integration test running harness against a local runtime instance with CUDA visible and validating that per-kernel metrics and spans appear in test Prometheus/Tempo endpoints.
- Perf regression gating: run full harness and assert that p50 change < 5% and p99 < 10% when sampling enabled.
